title: IELTS Academic 19 - Listening Test 3 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

12:49ANNOUNCER: Part 3. You will hear a trainee science teacher called Clare talking about her practical teaching work to another trainee called Jake.
13:00ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
13:40ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
13:45JAKE: Hi, Clare. How are you getting on with the practical teaching?
13:53CLARE: It's harder than I expected, but I've got some great classes. How about you?
13:58JAKE: Not brilliant. I'm really struggling with my Year 12 science class.
14:03CLARE: Are they hard to control?
14:05JAKE: Well, I don't have discipline problems as such. It's just that they don't seem to think that science has anything to do with their lives. It's depressing. But there's no real engagement.
14:22CLARE: Right. And as part of my teaching practice, I have to design an experiment for them to do. I was wondering about something on the children's diets, you know, asking them to record what they eat and maybe linking it to their state of health.
14:37JAKE: Mmm. Let's think. So your methodology would involve the children recording what they eat... OK, but you'd also need to have access to the children's medical records, and I don't think people would be happy about that; confidentiality would be an issue. If you could get the right data, the conclusions might be significant, but I suspect it's not going to be easy.
15:02CLARE: Right. Have you thought about doing an experiment using animals? Wouldn't that be upsetting for the children?
15:09JAKE: Well, the animals don't have to be harmed in any way. It could just be an experiment where they're given a certain diet and the effects are observed.
15:19CLARE: Would I have to get permission to use these animals?
15:22JAKE: Yes, you'd have to submit an outline of the experiment and fill in a form, but it's quite straightforward.
15:30CLARE: But if we found out that, say, a particular diet affects the health of animals, the same thing wouldn't necessarily be true for people, would it? JAKE: No, that's true. But the findings for any experiment are going to be limited. It's inevitable.
15:45CLARE: I suppose so. So what animals could I use to investigate the effects of diet? Mice?
15:52JAKE: Yes. You'd need experimental mice – ones that have been specially bred for experiments. OK, so what will your experiment be investigating exactly?
16:04CLARE: Well, something to do with nutrition. So maybe we could look at food supplements... things like extra iron and extra protein, and their impact on health.
16:15JAKE: Mmm. That might be rather broad. Maybe just look at the effects of one supplement, like sugar, on the health of the mice?
16:24CLARE: In fact, maybe the focus could be on whether mice can control their own diet. So, what happens when they have access to more sugar, that they don't really need? Exactly. Do they eat it or do they decide to leave it?
16:38JAKE: Great. Then later on, you could do a follow-up experiment adding another variable. Like, you could give some of the mice the chance to be more active, running on a wheel or something, and the others just sit around and don't do much.
16:54CLARE: Or I could repeat the experiment but change the type of food I provided... or use mice with a different genetic structure. But I think your idea would be more interesting. I might think about that some more.
17:12ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
17:43ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
17:51CLARE: So can I talk through a possible procedure for the experiment where mice are given a sugar supplement?
17:57JAKE: Sure. I did a similar experiment in college actually.
18:00CLARE: Great. So how many mice would I need?
18:04JAKE: I'd say about 12. And all young ones, not a mixture of old and young.
18:10CLARE: OK. And I'd need two groups of equal sizes, so six in each group. And how would I tell them apart? I suppose I could put some sort of tag on one group... or just mark them in some way?
18:25JAKE: You could use food colouring, that wouldn't hurt them.
18:28CLARE: Perfect. Then each group would go into a separate cage, and one group, let's call them group A, would be the control group. So they'd just have ordinary mouse food. I suppose you can buy that?
18:42JAKE: Yes, it comes in dry pellets. And the other group would have the same as the first group, but they'd also have the extra sugar.
18:50CLARE: Would you just give them straight sugar? It might be better to give them something like cereal with it.
18:56JAKE: Mmm. Then you'd need to weigh the mice, I should think once a week. And you'd need an electronic balance.
19:03CLARE: But we can't hold them on the balance, or it'd affect the reading.
19:08JAKE: Exactly. So you need something called a weighing chamber to stop the mice from running away. It sounds complicated, but actually you can just use a plastic box with holes in the top.
19:20CLARE: OK. So once we've measured the weight gain of each mouse, we can work out the average for each group, as well as the standard deviation. And then see where we go from there. That sounds cool, I think the students will enjoy it.
19:36JAKE: Yes. One thing...
19:42ANNOUNCER: That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three.

groups.title: Questions 26–30
groups.instructions:
Complete the flowchart below.
Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 26–30.

q21.text: How does Clare feel about the students in her Year 12 science class?
options: A. worried that they are not making progress
B. challenged by their poor behaviour in class
C. frustrated at their lack of interest in the subject

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (frustrated at their lack of interest in the subject)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'they don't seem to think that science has anything to do with their lives. It's depressing... no real engagement.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Clare nói rõ 'don't have discipline problems as such' (không có vấn đề về kỷ luật) nên loại B; 'results weren't too bad' nên loại A.

q22.text: How does Jake react to Clare's suggestion about an experiment based on children's diet?
options: A. He is concerned that the results might not be meaningful.
B. He feels some of the data might be difficult to obtain.
C. He suspects that the conclusions might be upsetting.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (He feels some of the data might be difficult to obtain)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'you'd also need to have access to the children's medical records, and I don't think people would be happy about that; confidentiality would be an issue... not going to be easy.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'need access to medical records / confidentiality / not going to be easy' = difficult to obtain.

q23.text: What problem do they agree may be involved in an experiment involving animals?
options: A. Any results may not apply to humans.
B. It may be complicated to get permission.
C. Students may not be happy about animal experiments.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (Any results may not apply to humans)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'the same thing wouldn't necessarily be true for people, would it? JAKE: No, that's true.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Về giấy phép (permission), Jake nói 'quite straightforward' (rất đơn giản) nên loại B.

q24.text: What question do they decide the experiment should address?
options: A. Are mice capable of controlling their food intake?
B. Does an increase in sugar lead to health problems?
C. How much do supplements of different kinds affect health?

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (Are mice capable of controlling their food intake?)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'maybe the focus could be on whether mice can control their own diet. So, what happens when they have access to more sugar... Do they eat it or do they decide to leave it?'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'control their own diet' = controlling their food intake.

q25.text: Clare might also consider doing another experiment involving
options: A. other types of food supplement.
B. different genetic strains of mice.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (varying amounts of exercise)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'give some of the mice the chance to be more active, running on a wheel or something, and the others just sit around... CLARE: I think your idea would be more interesting. I might think about that some more.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'more active, running on a wheel vs sit around' = varying amounts of exercise.

q26.text: Choose mice which are all the same
q26.stepTitle: Choose mice which are all the same

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (age)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I'd say about 12. And all young ones, not a mixture of old and young.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'all young ones, not old and young' = same age.

q27.text: Divide the mice into two groups, each with a different
q27.stepTitle: Divide the mice into two groups, each with a different

steps: • Đáp án đúng: H (colour)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'CLARE: how would I tell them apart? ... JAKE: You could use food colouring, that wouldn't hurt them.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'use food colouring' = each with a different colour.

q28.text: Feed group B the same, but also sugar contained in
q28.stepTitle: Feed group B the same, but also sugar contained in

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (cereal)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Would you just give them straight sugar? It might be better to give them something like cereal with it.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'sugar contained in cereal'.

q29.text: Place them in a weighing chamber to prevent
q29.stepTitle: Place them in a weighing chamber to prevent

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (escape)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'So you need something called a weighing chamber to stop the mice from running away.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'stop the mice from running away' = prevent escape.
• Đáp án đúng: F (calculations)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'we can work out the average for each group, as well as the standard deviation.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'work out average and standard deviation' = calculations.
